intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that vitelliform macular dystrophy-4 (VMD4) is caused by heterozygous or homozygous mutation in the IMPG1 gene (602870) on chromosome 6q14.1.

checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that IMPG1 mutations cause both autosomal-dominant and -recessive forms of VMD
checks.explanation: The abstract shows that IMPG1 mutations cause dominant and recessive VMD, with homozygous and compound heterozygous recessive cases. It never uses the name 'VMD4' and never says 'heterozygous' for the dominant cases; that is only implied by the inheritance pattern.

checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in IMPG1 cause vitelliform macular dystrophies.
checks.explanation: The chromosome location is standard nomenclature added to the gene named in the paper.

paragraphs.text: Vitelliform macular dystrophies are inherited retinal dystrophies. They are characterized by yellow, round deposits visible on fundus examination (Manes et al., 2013). Affected individuals have reported central vision loss that progressed slowly over years (Brandl et al., 2017). VMD4 is a form of adult-onset vitelliform macular dystrophy caused by mutation in IMPG1 (Meunier et al., 2014). IMPG1 encodes the SPACR protein, a component of the rod and cone photoreceptor extracellular matrix, and the disorder can show autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive inheritance (Manes et al., 2013).

paragraphs.text: Manes et al. (2013) reported both autosomal dominant and autosomal recessive transmission of VMD4. The same IMPG1 mutation was found in all 3 families with autosomal dominant disease. Of the 2 families with autosomal recessive disease, affected individuals in one were homozygous for an IMPG1 mutation and those in the other were compound heterozygous.

paragraphs.text: Vitelliform macular dystrophy is genetically heterogeneous. Meunier et al. (2014) identified IMPG2 as a causal gene, and mutation in IMPG2 causes VMD5. IMPG2 encodes SPACRCAN, a proteoglycan related to SPACR, the IMPG1 protein (Brandl et al., 2017). Other forms of vitelliform macular dystrophy are caused by mutation in the BEST1 or PRPH2 gene (Manes et al., 2013).

checks.claim: Vitelliform macular dystrophy is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Although many BMD and some AVMD cases harbor mutations in BEST1 or PRPH2, the underlying genetic cause remains unknown for many affected individuals.
checks.explanation: Several causal genes (BEST1, PRPH2 and IMPG1) mean the condition is genetically heterogeneous.

paragraphs.text: Manes et al. (2013) studied families with vitelliform macular dystrophy. In a large family with autosomal dominant disease, they used gene mapping and whole-exome sequencing to identify a c.713T-G mutation in the IMPG1 gene, resulting in a leu238-to-arg (L238R) substitution. The same mutation was then found in 2 other families with autosomal dominant disease. In a family with autosomal recessive disease, 2 affected individuals were homozygous for a splice-site mutation in IMPG1 (c.807+1G-T).
